Re: Member appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Taylor Ellison  
Member ID: W423241591  
Reference number: POC-C4BC2EBAC7-30163  
Requested service: Shoulder labral/instability repair  
CPT: 29806  
Denial date: August 14, 2026  

Dear PacificSource Appeals and Grievances Department:

I appeal the denial of prior authorization for shoulder labral and instability repair, CPT 29806. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The records do document an adequate and appropriately directed trial, and they also establish persistent symptomatic instability with objective structural pathology and substantial functional impairment.

Taylor has experienced nine months of recurrent shoulder-instability episodes with apprehension. Conservative treatment included 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 1, 2026, through July 22, 2026, with 18 visits completed. The therapy specifically addressed rotator-cuff and scapular-stabilizer strengthening and included activity modification. The completed course is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taylor also used NSAIDs for approximately four months during symptom flares. An injection was not indicated for the underlying instability. Thus, the treatment history includes an extended supervised rehabilitation program, activity modification, and medication management, rather than an absence of conservative care.

The clinical records further demonstrate that conservative care did not resolve the problem:

- Three anterior shoulder dislocations have occurred since symptom onset.
- The most recent dislocation required reduction in the emergency department.
- Taylor continues to experience apprehension and avoids overhead reaching.
- Taylor cannot return to work involving lifting.
- Examination shows positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing.
- The June 3, 2026, MR arthrogram shows an anteroinferior labral tear consistent with a Bankart lesion, a small Hill-Sachs lesion, and less than 10 percent glenoid bone loss.
- The rotator cuff is intact, and the examination documents full strength.

These findings establish symptomatic anterior glenohumeral instability with a structural labral injury and recurrent dislocations despite documented conservative management. The requested repair is directed at the documented Bankart lesion and recurrent instability. The records therefore address the stated basis for denial and support medical necessity for surgical stabilization.

There are no documented active infection, untreated substance-use issue, smoking, or other listed clinical concern that would explain denial of the requested procedure. Taylor’s BMI is 29.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29806. If PacificSource maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical criteria and policy version applied to this request, identify the specific criterion that PacificSource believes was not met, and explain why the documented 16-week supervised therapy course, 18 completed visits, medication treatment, recurrent dislocations, emergency reduction, objective examination findings, and MR arthrogram findings were insufficient.

Please associate this appeal with reference number POC-C4BC2EBAC7-30163. I request review of all records submitted with the original authorization request, the physical therapy discharge note, the MR arthrogram report, examination findings, and the orthopedic surgeon’s medical-necessity documentation.

This appeal may be submitted through InTouch using Ask a Question or by email to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com. Please confirm receipt and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Taylor Ellison
